profile.workplace: Verbena, a tasting room on East 6th
profile.commute: a mint green Vespa called Tilde
profile.hobby: Sunday pickup soccer at Zilker, plays left back

memories.text: I feed the sourdough starter, which is named Bartleby, at a quarter past six every morning with fifty grams of rye and fifty of water.
We did a hundred and twelve covers on a Thursday, which is thirty more than the room is supposed to hold, and the dish pit never once fell behind.
Decided to cut the tasting menu from nine courses to seven and killed the beet dish, replacing it with charred fennel and buttermilk.
Argued with Renata on the line about whether the fennel needs the anchovy, and we settled it by making both and letting the dishwasher pick.
The walk-in drifted up to forty-four degrees overnight and I moved every dairy container to the reach-in before the repair guy arrived at eleven.
The koji batch is on day four and smells like pineapple, which is exactly right, and I am pulling it Sunday to make the chickpea miso.
Played left back at Zilker and got nutmegged twice by a fifteen year old whose father was standing on the touchline enjoying it enormously.
A regular at the counter asked what the burnt-looking crumb on the fennel was, and when I said toasted milk solids he ordered a second plate.
Decided to re-handle my two hundred and forty millimetre gyuto in white oak instead of buying a new knife, and ordered the epoxy for it.
Tilde would not start outside the loading dock and it turned out to be the fuel line, so I pushed the Vespa four blocks in the heat.
There are three chile plants on the windowsill above the prep sink and only the serrano has produced anything worth picking.
Burned the back of my left wrist on the salamander during service and finished the night with a wet towel wrapped around it.
Decided to move family meal from four thirty to three so the front of house can eat before the polish, and told everyone by taping a note to the pass.
The produce rep told me the peach crop from the Fredericksburg grower is done in ten days, so I booked the last two cases for Saturday.
Closed out with a Topo Chico and three limes on the back step and watched the bar next door lose a whole rack of glassware in one crash.
Got to the market at seven twenty and the okra was already picked over, so I bought eight pounds of Sungold tomatoes to make up the menu.
My mother's recipe card for pork vindaloo is taped inside the spice cupboard door and the vinegar quantity on it has been crossed out twice.
Decided to put the seven course menu on a single card with no prices listed on the back, and to have Renata read the wine pairings aloud instead.
